title: Repair is dispatched only against evidence on the exact current candidate
summary: Before repair work is re-dispatched for a defect recorded against a superseded candidate, the defect signature is re-checked against the exact current accepted candidate; historical verdicts and administrative labels are not evidence of an open defect.

protected.asset: Accepted work and the repair budget of an automated dispatch pipeline
protected.failure: A stale verdict or administrative label on an old candidate triggers redundant repair, or reverts later accepted work that already absorbed the defect.

rationale: An unattended controller that turns stored records into repair dispatches must distinguish the identity of the candidate a verdict belongs to from the label attached to it. A negative review verdict names the candidate it examined; later accepted changes may absorb or relocate the defect, and an administrative status (done, blocked) is bookkeeping rather than technical evidence in either direction. Re-deriving applicability from the current candidate identifier before scheduling repair prevents replaying history as if it were current state.

variants.description: Re-run the minimal failing check named in the historical verdict against the exact current candidate identifier; dispatch repair only when the same signature reproduces.
Where re-checking is disproportionate, hold the candidate repair and request a current applicability statement from the owning controller instead of dispatching.

verification.method: Pick one historical negative verdict, identify the exact candidate it examined, and confirm the dispatch path requires a current-candidate re-check before repair is scheduled; walk one defect that was absorbed by later accepted work through the same path and confirm it is not dispatched.
verification.evidence: The historical verdict's candidate identifier, the current candidate identifier, and the re-check outcome for both cases; no full transcripts.

rollback.method: Withdraw the gate to restore direct dispatch; the re-check itself mutates no state.
rollback.safety: The re-check is read-only against the current candidate.

failure_modes: The re-check compares against a moving branch tip instead of an exact candidate identifier.
An administrative completion label is read as proof that the defect is gone.
A defect signature too vague to reproduce makes the re-check inconclusive; this must surface as undecided, never as a pass.

hermes_versions.notes: Operational practice control: the range records the builds whose dispatch surfaces the procedure was read against, not a versioned platform feature.

last_verification.notes: General operational synthesis from recorded practice with private detail removed; no specific public incident is claimed.

references: General operational synthesis from recorded practice; no publicly verifiable incident is cited.
